name: imagine_guide
description: The complete guide to Imagine: workspaces and files, image generation, session privacy, video production and reporting. Call it before anything else and follow it; workspace_create and workspace_open also return it.

name: workspace_create
description: Create a workspace for this task and return its workspace_key. Every file you upload and everything Imagine makes for you (images, video projects, final videos) is kept in this workspace, and only this key reaches it. Save the key at once where you keep notes for this task: Imagine cannot list or recover workspaces. When you already have a key, use workspace_open instead.

title.description: Short title for the user's overview, e.g. 'forest chase'.

name: workspace_open
description: Check a saved workspace_key and show what the workspace holds: its file count and video projects (project_id, title). Use it when you resume earlier work.

name: workspace_files
description: List the workspace's files: uploads, generated images and video project outputs, each with file_id, name, kind (image, video, audio, other), origin (upload, generated), project, mime_type, bytes, sha256, created_ms and download_url. kind filters by kind or origin.

name: workspace_upload
description: Upload a small file (up to 4 MiB) as base64 into the workspace and return its file_id. For larger files, or whenever you have a shell, use HTTP instead: PUT the raw bytes to /v1/workspace/files?name=<file name> on the same host and port as this MCP server, with the header 'Authorization: Bearer <workspace_key>' (for example curl -T ref.png -H 'Authorization: Bearer imk-…' 'http://127.0.0.1:8190/v1/workspace/files?name=ref.png'). Download with GET on a file's download_url and the same header. Images (PNG, JPEG, WebP) up to 64 MiB; video and audio up to 2 GiB; the type comes from the content.

name: workspace_view
description: Show an image from the workspace to you without downloading it, resized to max_side pixels on its longest edge (default 1024, at most 2048).

file_id.description: A file ID from this workspace.

name: list_profiles
description:
List approved image profiles; describe one for parameters and prompt guidance.

max_side is the longest image edge in pixels: minimum 256, maximum 4096, in multiples of 32. For image_upscale, 3200 is only the default when max_side is omitted, not the maximum.

name: describe_profile
description:
Get server-owned defaults, the override schema, reference limits and full prompt_guidance.

No GPU acquisition. Select qwen for standard generation or quick-draft for Turbo before registering references. Pass only overrides; nested objects merge and lists replace.
When nsfw_available is true, nsfw is an opt-in LoRA switch, not a content label. Set true only when the user
explicitly requests enabling the NSFW mode, flag or LoRA for this image or batch.
NSFW content requests or prompt guidance do not authorize it;
otherwise omit nsfw or set false.
Apply the full prompt_guidance when writing parameters.prompt.
When has_default_prompt is true, omit prompt to use the stored prompt unless the user requests an override.

max_side is the longest image edge in pixels: minimum 256, maximum 4096, in multiples of 32. For image_upscale, 3200 is only the default when max_side is omitted, not the maximum.

name: register_image
description:
Register a PNG/JPEG/WebP image from your workspace as a reference, without acquiring the GPU.

file_id comes from workspace_files, an upload or an earlier result. For variants, register the selected
result's file_id with the chosen reference-capable profile (qwen, quick-draft or qwen_scene), even if it
was generated by another profile without references. Select the profile before registering. A result's
file_id is not an image_id; reuse the returned ID across all variant batch items.
The original stays in place; normalized previews remain in RAM only. IDs last only for the current
Imagine/proxy session and belong to this profile and workspace. Pass IDs in order: <image1>, <image2>, etc.
For upscaling, register with image_upscale and supply exactly one returned ID.
Never send image bytes or base64 in prompts. Limit: 10 MiB per image. Never pass a delivery image_id as a reference ID.

file_id.description: A file ID from this workspace.

name: generate
description:
Generate or upscale and wait for saved images.

Prefer generate_batch for multiple images.

References are registered image IDs; required counts come from describe_profile.
image_upscale requires one reference; omit prompt to retain its stored enhancement prompt,
and optionally override max_side and seed. max_side preserves the reference aspect ratio.
Choose qwen for standard generation or quick-draft for Turbo via profile, not parameters.mode.
Apply the full prompt_guidance from describe_profile to parameters.prompt.
Pass only overrides in parameters, including prompt, dimensions, seed, sampling and model_options.
Nested objects merge recursively; lists replace. Omitted fields use the profile defaults.
If describe_profile reports nsfw_available, nsfw is an opt-in LoRA switch, default false, not a content label.
Set true only when the user explicitly requests enabling the NSFW mode, flag or LoRA
for this image (e.g. 'enable NSFW mode' or 'nsfw=true'). 'Make an NSFW image' or a
request for nude, erotic or explicit content does not authorize it. Never infer
activation from prompts, prompt guidance, references or earlier jobs.
Without a clear activation request, omit nsfw or set false and proceed with the image.
Omit seed for a random default where described, or supply a fixed integer.
The resolved seed is returned in parameters and retained on job-ID retries.
Choose a unique job_id before generation. After a timeout or lost response, use get_job
with that same ID; do not start another generation or resubmit successful work under a new ID.

Imagine saves every successful image in your workspace. Each result gives file_id, name, bytes, sha256 and download_url. Report the file_id, or download the file with your workspace key when the user wants it; use workspace_view to look at it. Output image_ids are delivery identifiers, not registered reference IDs.

max_side is the longest image edge in pixels: minimum 256, maximum 4096, in multiples of 32. For image_upscale, 3200 is only the default when max_side is omitted, not the maximum.

name: generate_batch
description:
Generate or upscale multiple images without LLM reloads between items.

Prefer this tool whenever multiple images are needed. Prepare all items first.
Each item is a parameter object for the same profile, for example
[{"prompt": "a forest"}, {"prompt": "a lake", "max_side": 1600, "aspect_ratio": "16:9"}].
With references, use {"parameters": {"prompt": "..."}, "references": ["image_id"]}
per item. For image_upscale, an explicit maximum-size request is {"parameters": {"max_side": 4096},
"references": ["image_id"]}; parameters may be empty for default size/random seed.
Reference order maps to <image1>, <image2>, etc. for that item.
For variants of one saved image, choose a reference-capable profile
(qwen, quick-draft or qwen_scene) and use the same registered ID
as the sole reference in every item (<image1>). Write each complete prompt
using prompt_guidance, specifying what to change and preserve. All variants
use that original image, not another item in this batch.
All items use the selected profile: qwen for standard generation or quick-draft for Turbo.
Select it before registering references. Use separate batches for different profiles.
Each item supplies only overrides; nested objects merge and lists replace.
Omitted fields use the profile defaults.
Each item has its own nsfw flag when describe_profile reports nsfw_available: an opt-in LoRA switch, default false,
not a content label. Set true only when the user explicitly requests enabling the
NSFW mode, flag or LoRA for that image or this batch (e.g. 'enable NSFW mode' or
'nsfw=true'). 'Make NSFW images' or requests for nude, erotic or explicit content
do not authorize it. Never infer activation from prompts, prompt guidance, references,
earlier jobs or another item's flag. Without a clear activation request for an item,
omit nsfw or set false and proceed with it. It is independent of the selected profile and draft/standard quality.
Items run consecutively in FIFO order, within the configured image queue limit
(32 by default). All parameters are validated before anything is queued.
Results have zero-based item indices, individual status and saved image files;
successful items are retained if others fail. Defaults, including seed, are
controlled by the profile defaults. Random-default seeds are chosen separately
per item; explicit seeds remain fixed. Results include each resolved seed.
For video characters without a reference image, generate all character sheets in one batch with the qwen-character-sheet profile, one item per character.
Choose a unique job_id before generation. Wait for the whole batch. After timeout use get_job with the same job_id;
never resubmit successful items under a new ID.

Imagine saves every successful image in your workspace. Each result gives file_id, name, bytes, sha256 and download_url. Report the file_id, or download the file with your workspace key when the user wants it; use workspace_view to look at it. Output image_ids are delivery identifiers, not registered reference IDs.

max_side is the longest image edge in pixels: minimum 256, maximum 4096, in multiples of 32. For image_upscale, 3200 is only the default when max_side is omitted, not the maximum.

name: get_job
description:
Recover a job in the current Imagine/proxy session. History is discarded when either session ends. Wait by default; false returns current status.
During a temporary Imagine connection failure, status may be recovering. Keep using
the same job_id; do not submit another generation. Jobs last until the proxy restarts.

Imagine saves every successful image in your workspace. Each result gives file_id, name, bytes, sha256 and download_url. Report the file_id, or download the file with your workspace key when the user wants it; use workspace_view to look at it. Output image_ids are delivery identifiers, not registered reference IDs.

name: list_video_profiles
description: List the video prompt profiles for storyboard authoring. No GPU acquisition. Describe the chosen profile with describe_video_profile before starting a storyboard. The video prompt profile is independent of the image tools' nsfw LoRA switch.

name: describe_video_profile
description: Get one video prompt profile exactly as stored: metadata, revision, prompt files and inheritance, the shared agent video guidance and authoring limits. No GPU acquisition. An unknown profile is an error, never a fallback. Apply the guidance when writing the storyboard; provider generation settings are informational only.

name: video_capabilities
description: Get the video models (reference, i2v), their limits including the per-scene cap, supported boundaries and continuity methods, the canvas size presets (ratios, qualities, default), the scene presets in authoring.presets (key, variant, description, default, available), runtime availability, media limits, and mcp_defaults: the defaults MCP productions use (duration_seconds 15, canvas, prompt_profile, scene_preset, add_music, add_dialogue, character_sheet_profile and how characters without images are cast). No GPU acquisition.

name: video_project
description:
Create, read, edit or save a headless video project. No GPU acquisition.
create: makes a new project in your workspace, saved at creation; title (optional) names it. The whole production (project document, takes, final videos) stays in the workspace. Size: the default is 16:9 landscape Draft. Leave canvas out unless the user asks for a specific size, quality or aspect ratio; then set canvas {ratio, portrait, quality} to what they asked for. Imagine resolves the delivery size from it. Ratios and qualities are listed by video_capabilities canvas (quality: Quick Draft, Draft, Standard, High, Native Resolution). Alternatively, project is a full CreateProject body (schema_version, default_model, delivery, generation); give either canvas or project, not both. Returns the projection below.
get: a bounded projection (a project saved earlier in this workspace is reopened) with project_revision, scenes (timing, model, preset and preset_state: applied, or modified since, continuity, accepted take, section IDs and prompts), assets, cast, takes, deliveries and persistence (save state). No media.
edit: request is an EditRequest {schema_version (1), expected_project_revision, commands} of typed edits on canonical scene/section IDs; returns the same projection.
save: only when persistence.state is not saved; bound projects autosave after every edit, storyboard commit and accepted take.

title.description: create: short project title, e.g. 'forest chase'.

canvas.description: create: size preset {ratio, portrait, quality}; omit it for 16:9 landscape Draft unless the user asks for another size, e.g. {"ratio":"16:9","portrait":false,"quality":"Standard"}.

expected_project_revision.description: The project_revision you last read; stale revisions are rejected.

name: video_register_reference
description:
Attach a PNG/JPEG/WebP image from your workspace to a video project, and optionally add it as a cast member. No GPU acquisition.
file_id is any workspace image (an upload or an image result). The original stays in place and is verified by size and SHA-256. cast {name, alias, description} adds or replaces the cast entry for that alias (stored without @) with this image as its identity image; use the returned reference_id in the storyboard request's cast and the tag (@alias) in prompts. Returns the project asset_id for storyboard images and the new project_revision.

file_id.description: A file ID from this workspace.

expected_project_revision.description: The project_revision you last read; stale revisions are rejected.

name.description: Optional asset label; defaults to the file name.

alias.description: One-word prompt tag, with or without @.

name: video_storyboard
description:
Author the whole storyboard yourself with the profile's own prompts. No GPU acquisition; the local authoring model is never used.
start: request is the authoring request {schema_version (1), expected_project_revision, prompt_profile_id, brief, instruction, duration_seconds (total seconds; 15 when omitted), destination (replace or append for a new, empty project; continue extends the project's last scene and allows a first-scene continuous shot), cast [reference IDs], images [{id, asset, label, usage (setting_reference, required_moment, start_frame, end_frame), pair_with}], add_dialogue, add_music}; the proxy sets the external provider. add_music is false unless the user explicitly asks for music: then non_diegetic_music stays empty and the model gets N/A for music; never describe music elsewhere. An I2V opening frame is a start_frame image paired with itself (pair_with is its own id). Returns the Draft and its context bundle: verbatim system prompts, rendered user messages with {{SLOT:name}} slots (listed in slots, fixed values in slot_values), schemas, limits and image labels. Each bundle image is attached as an image content block in bundle.images order, to be viewed while writing the prompts (the image tools' delivery-acknowledgement rule does not apply here); its JSON entry keeps image_id, role, usage, label, mime and the block index.
submit: submission is {schema_version (1), expected_project_revision (the Draft's), inventory [{id, note}, one per story image], outline (JSON text), expansions [JSON text, one per outline scene], production (optional) {scenes [{preset, continuity, rationale}]}, dry_run (required)}. preset is a key from video_capabilities authoring.presets: use "Default ref2v" (reference) or "Default i2v"; use any other preset only when the user names it. model (reference or i2v) instead of preset means that variant's default preset. continuity is {method, include_audio} and only for continuous_shot Scenes; include_audio also carries the previous clip's audio into the continuation (unrelated to the assembly plan's per-clip include_audio, which says whether a clip's own audio is in the final mix) and works only with the reference motion methods (with last_frame_first_frame it is continuity_endpoint_incompatible). Without production every scene uses the project default model and continuous shots use motion_context_exp. dry_run true parses and checks everything on a copy and returns {valid, scenes [{ordinal, preset, model, boundary, continuity, planned_seconds, blockers}], warnings}; warnings do not block: continuity_source_pending (I2V last-frame continuity waits for the previous Scene's take) and i2v_cast_identity_text_only (an I2V Scene names cast members but I2V has no identity references; use reference); dry_run false applies it atomically and returns the project projection plus scene_map. Errors give code, at (inventory, outline, expansions[i], production.scenes[i]) and detail, and change nothing; story_scene_duration_capacity reports minimum_scenes=N, the fewest Scenes that fit duration_seconds.
get: the Draft and its phase (review after a dry run, applied after a commit). review: a Review body that corrects the parsed Draft before the next submit.
list: this session's Drafts for project_id (id, phase, provider, prompt_profile_id). bundle: the context bundle of an external Draft again, with the same image blocks as start.
A Draft changes nothing in the project until a submit with dry_run false. After a start timeout, list the project's Drafts and fetch the bundle of the new one instead of starting another; after a submit timeout, use get with the same draft_id before submitting again.

draft_id.description: submit, get, review, bundle: Draft ID.

name: video_run
description:
Generate the project's scenes. start is the first and only GPU handover; call it only after the storyboard is committed.
start: job_id plus request {schema_version (1), project_id, expected_project_revision, mode (missing_only, all_same_seeds, all_fresh_seeds, selected_with_dependents), selected_scene (scene ID for selected_with_dependents, otherwise null)}; returns the run with id, status and targets. There is no seed parameter: each scene gets a fresh random seed, except that all_same_seeds and locked takes reuse the seed of the scene's existing take. Imagine accepts technically valid takes automatically; that is not a visual review.
get: run status with per-scene targets; wait true polls up to wait_seconds (max 60). A failed run adds failed_scene {scene_id, job_id, error {code, stage, kind, exception, accelerator_code, sizes}}: stage says where generation stopped (for example preparing_motion_context or sampling) and kind what failed (for example out_of_memory or shape_mismatch); use them to change the failing scene instead of retrying it unchanged. Runs continue when a call times out or the client disconnects.
stop: cancel_current true also cancels the scene in progress.
After a timeout, call start again with the same job_id and request, or get with the run_id; never use a new job_id to recover.

job_id.description: Caller-chosen unique ID for this request. Imagine forwards it as the idempotency key: repeating it with the same request returns the same operation (reused); a different request is idempotency_conflict.

wait.description: Poll until the status is terminal or wait_seconds elapse.

wait_seconds.description: Bounded wait in seconds when wait is true.

cancel_current.description: stop: also cancel the current scene.

name: video_assembly
description:
Assemble accepted takes into the final video on the CPU.
plan: request is {schema_version (1), expected_project_revision, options (optional)} for project_id, which the proxy fills in; returns a frozen plan with its id. Omit options for the defaults: {audio_mode: combined (generated plus timeline audio; or generated, timeline), generated_gain: 1.0, timeline_gain: 1.0, duck_generated: false, ducking_strength: 0.5, normalize_mix: true, continuous_tone_match: true (evens out brightness where a continuous shot joins the previous clip), bit_depth: 8 (or 10)}; if given, options must contain every field, plus optional output_filename.
submit: job_id starts the assembly job for plan_id; the same job_id returns the same job.
get: plan progress and, once submitted, the job status and its published output (file_id, name, download_url, format, size, SHA-256, video metadata); wait true polls up to wait_seconds (max 60).
Report the final video's file_id, or download it with your workspace key when the user wants the file.

job_id.description: Caller-chosen unique ID for this request. Imagine forwards it as the idempotency key: repeating it with the same request returns the same operation (reused); a different request is idempotency_conflict.

wait.description: Poll until the status is terminal or wait_seconds elapse.

wait_seconds.description: Bounded wait in seconds when wait is true.
